questions.question: Base changes the colour of the red litmus to ______.

• It tastes bitter and changes the colour of red litmus into blue. It reacts with acids to form salts.

• Litmus paper is a paper that is treated with a specific indicator which is a mixture of 10 to 15 natural dyes obtained from lichens.
 
• It is helpful in determining whether the solution is acidic or basic.

questions.question: In 1873, he founded the Satya-Shodhak Samaj. Who is referred to as 'he' here?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Jyotirao Phule__.

__
 
• Jyotibha Phule, the founder of Satyashodhak samaj Satyashodhak Samaj(Truth-seekers' Society) was a social reform society founded by Jyotirao Phule in Pune, Maharashtra, on 24 September 1873.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• Satyashodhak Samaj:-__

 __
 
• Satyashodhak Samaj (Truth-seekers' Society) was a social reform society founded by Jyotirao Phule in Pune, Maharashtra, on 24 September 1873.
 
• It espoused a mission of education and increased social rights and political access for underprivileged groups, focusing especially on women, Shudras, and Dalits, in Maharashtra.
 
• Jyotirao's wife Savitribai was the head of the women's section of society.
 
• The Samaj disbanded during the 1930s as leaders left to join the Indian National Congress party under Mahatma Gandhi. 
 
 
 
• ​Jyotirao Govindrao Phule:-__
 
 
• Jyotirao Govindrao Phule (11 April 1827 – 28 November 1890) was an Indian social activist, thinker, anti-caste social reformer, and writer from Maharashtra.
 
• His work extended to many fields, including the eradication of untouchability and the caste system, and women's emancipation.
 
• He revolted against the domination of the Brahmins and struggled for the rights of peasants and other low-caste people.
 
• Mahatma Jyotiba Phule was also a pioneer for women's education in India and fought for the education of girls throughout his life.
 
• He is believed to be the first Hindu to start an orphanage for unfortunate children.

• According to mythology, there is another river related to this confluence named Saraswati, which originates from Mana village of Badrinath.
 
• Devprayag is the place where the rivers Alaknanda & Bhagirathi are confluent.

questions.question: Personal Disposable income is money that is available for household consumption, ________ and spending after accounting for income tax.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** savings.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Disposable Personal Income Formula = Personal Income - Direct taxes + Consumption Expenditure + Savings__

 [IMAGE: https:https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Personal Disposable income:

 
 
• Disposable income or disposable personal income is an economic term that means the money that is available for household consumption, savings, and spending after accounting for income tax.
 
• ​It is an important indicator that is used by economists in determining the demand in an economy.
 
• It is used to estimate the overall state of the country’s economy.
 
 

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• In national accounts definitions, personal income minus personal current taxes equals disposable personal income. 
 
• Subtracting personal outlays yields personal (or, private) savings, hence the income left after paying away all the taxes is referred to as disposable income.
 
• For the economy or country, it is calculated as:
 
 
• National Income + All the Indirect Taxes + Transfers from other Countries.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides for 'protection against arrest and detention in certain cases’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Article 22.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• Article 22 - Protection against arrest and detention 

 
 
• No person, who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed of the grounds for such arrest nor shall he be denied the right to consult, and to be defended by a legal practitioner of his choice. 
 
• Every person, who is arrested and detained in custody is to be produced before the nearest Magistrate within a period of 24 hours of arrest and such person cannot be detained in custody beyond that period without the authority of a Magistrate.
 
• Article 22 is not available to an enemy alien and a person arrested or detained under a law providing for preventive detention (detention of a person without trial). 
 
• The detention of a person cannot exceed three months under the Preventive Detention Law.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Article 10 **of the Constitution of India states that Any person who is considered a citizen of India under any of the provisions of this Part shall continue to be citizens and will also be subject to any law made by the Parliament
 
• **Article 47** of the Constitution of India directs the State to raise the level of nutrition and the standard of living and to improve public health.
 
• ** Article 35** of the Constitution of India provides for the power of the Parliament to make laws with respect to any matter not enumerated in the Concurrent List or State List.

questions.question: Disadvantage of the industrial development is _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** pollution.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

**Here are some points to explain why industrial development is associated with pollution:**

__
 
• Industrial development involves the establishment and **growth of factories, power plants, and other facilities** that produce goods and services on a large scale. These facilities **require energy, raw materials, and other inputs, which are often extracted from the environment**. As a result, industrial development **can lead to various types of pollution, such as air pollution, water pollution, and soil pollution.**
 
• **Air pollution** is caused by the emission of harmful gases and particles into the atmosphere from industrial processes such as the burning of fossil fuels, transportation, and manufacturing. This can lead to respiratory problems, heart disease, and other health issues for humans and animals.
 
• ** Water pollution **is caused by the release of toxic chemicals, heavy metals, and other contaminants into rivers, lakes, and oceans. This can harm aquatic life and make water unsafe for human consumption.
 
• ** Soil pollution** is caused by the accumulation of hazardous waste, pesticides, and other chemicals in the soil. This can affect the quality of crops and livestock, and also contaminate groundwater.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sustainable development **is a concept that refers to the development of an economy that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs. While industrial development can contribute to economic growth, it may not always be sustainable in the long run due to the environmental and social costs associated with it.
 
• ** High revenue collection,** refers to the financial benefits that can be generated by industrial development through taxes, fees, and other sources of income. While this can be a positive outcome, it should not be the sole focus of industrial development as it may come at the expense of the environment and public health.
 
• ** Economic growth **is often cited as a key benefit of industrial development as it can create jobs, increase productivity, and raise living standards. However, economic growth should not be pursued at the expense of environmental and social sustainability.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of indirect tax?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** G.S.T.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **G.S.T. (Goods and Services Tax) is an example of an indirect tax because it is imposed on the final consumer, but is collected by businesses at each stage of production and distribution.**
 
• ** Indirect taxes** are those that are** imposed on goods and services** and are ultimately paid by the consumer, while **direct taxes are those that are imposed on individuals or entities and are paid directly by them**.
 
• **Gift tax** is a tax on the transfer of property by one individual to another, and is usually paid by the person giving the gift.
 
 
• Gift tax is a direct tax, as it is imposed directly on the person giving the gift.
 
 
 
• **Corporation tax** for firms is a tax on the profits of the company and is usually paid by the company itself.
 
 
• Corporation tax for firms is also a direct tax, as it is imposed on the profits of the company.
 
 
 
• ** Property tax** is a tax on the value of property and is usually paid by the owner of the property. 
 
 
• Property tax is a direct tax, as it is imposed on the owner of the property.

questions.question: Limestone, chalk and marble are different forms of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Calcium carbonate__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Calcium carbonate and its forms: 

 
 
• In nature, calcium carbonate occurs in the forms of chalk, limestone, and marble.
 
• Limestone, chalk, and marble are all sedimentary rocks that are composed mainly of calcium carbonate.
 
• Limestone is a sedimentary rock that forms from the accumulation of calcium carbonate shells and skeletons of marine organisms.
 
• Chalk is a soft, white, porous rock that is made up of the microscopic remains of marine plankton.
 
• Formation:
 
 
• ​The skeletal remains of dead sea animals sink to the seabed. Over millions of years, layer build-up and pressure from the top layer changes the bottom layer into chalk. 
 
 
 
• Earth movements due to earthquakes lift the layer of chalk to the Earth's surface. 
 
• The earth's movements can also cause the layers to sink further. Thus, high pressure and heat cause the chalk to turn into much harder limestone. 
 
• The limestone deposit may stay below the Earth for a longer time and due to higher pressure and temperature, the limestone turns to marble.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Calcium Oxide (CaO), commonly known as quicklime or burnt lime, is a widely used chemical compound.

 
 
• It is a white, caustic, alkaline, crystalline solid at room temperature.
 
 
 
• Calcium phosphate [Ca₃(PO₄)₂] is fundamental to the formation of teeth and bone.
 
 
• Calcium phosphate is a calcium salt of phosphoric acid. It is also known as Calcium phosphate tribasic or Tricalcium Phosphate.
 
 
 
• Calcium Hydroxide [Ca(OH)₂] is also known as Slaked lime.
 
 
• It is a white powder or colourless crystal which is obtained when quicklime (calcium oxide) is mixed with water.

questions.question: In which sport is the field often oval with a rectangular area in the middle, that is 22 yards (20.12 metres) by 10 feet (3.04 metres) wide?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Cricket.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cricket,** **as it is the only sport that has an oval field with a rectangular area in the middle called the pitch, which measures 22 yards by 10 feet wide**.

 
 
• The pitch is where the bowler delivers the ball to the batsman, who tries to hit it and score runs by running back and forth between the wickets at either end of the pitch.
 
• Cricket is a popular sport in many countries, especially in South Asia, Australia, and England, and is known for its long duration, strategic gameplay, and unique terminology.
 
• The distance between the two wickets is normally 20.12 meters.
 
• The height of stamps is generally 71.1 cm above the ground.
 
• The bowling crease should be 2.64m in length and must be marked at each end of the pitch in line with the wickets.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Lawn tennis is played on a rectangular court with a net in the middle and involves hitting a ball over the net with a racket.
 
• Basketball is played on a rectangular court with two hoops on either end and involves shooting a ball into the opposing team's hoop to score points.
 
• Volleyball is played on a rectangular court with a net in the middle and involves hitting a ball over the net with your hands to score points.

questions.question: The ________ is the sole link of communication between the Cabinet and the Governor.

options.text: Chairman of State Public Service Commission

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Chief Minister.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Chief Minister communicates to the Governor all decisions of the Council of Ministers related to the administration of the affairs of the State.
 
• The Chief Minister communicates to the Governor the proposals for legislation.
 
• The Chief Minister participates in the meetings of the National Development Council.
 
• But it's not the constitutional duty of the Chief Minister and the National Development Council is a statutory body. 
 
• The Chief Minister submits for the consideration of the Council of Ministers any matter on which decision has been taken by a minister but which has not been considered by the council as if the Governor requires.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__ 

__
 
• Article 167 (Constitutional Duties) 

 
 
• Duties of Chief Minister as respects the furnishing of information to the Governor, etc It shall be the duty of the Chief Minister of each State
 
• To communicate to the Governor of the State all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to the administration of the affairs of the State and proposals for legislation;
 
• To furnish such information relating to the administration of the affairs of the State and proposals for legislation as the Governor may call for; and
 
• If the Governor so requires, to submit for the consideration of the Council of Ministers any matter on which a decision has been taken by a Minister but which has not been considered by the Council
 
 
 
• Duties of Chief Minister
 
 
• The leader of the legislative assembly: In the matter of determining the internal policies of the State, the decision of the Chief Minister is final. He remains responsible to the Legislative Assembly for the acts performed by the State Council of Ministers. He comes to the rescue of a minister if he faces any difficulty during the debates in the Assembly. He has to bear the responsibility of getting the important bills passed. He has to keep good relations with the people and see that efforts are made to improve the condition of the state.
 
• The Chief Adviser to the Governor: The governor is advised by the Chief Minister so that he can perform his functions. The Chief Minister acts as a bridge of communication between the Governor and the Council of Ministers. On the advice of the Chief Minister, the Governor performs his tasks in matters like summoning, proroguing or dissolving the Legislative Assembly.
 
• The Leader of the Council of Ministers: The constitution gives supremacy to the Chief Minister by making him the leader of the ministers, thus it is his responsibility to maintain unity among the ministers. He monitors the working of all the ministers and oversees the meetings of the Council of Ministers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• **Advocate General:** The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor and serves as the chief legal advisor to the state government. He/she represents the state government in various legal matters and provides legal advice on matters related to the state's administration.
 
• **Chief Election Commissioner:** The Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by the President of India and is responsible for conducting free and fair elections in the state. He/she ensures that the election process is conducted in an unbiased and transparent manner and takes necessary steps to prevent malpractices during the election process.
 
• **Chairman of State Public Service Commission: **The Chairman of State Public Service Commission is responsible for conducting recruitment exams for various state government jobs. He/she ensures that the recruitment process is conducted in a fair and transparent manner and selects the most suitable candidates for the job.

questions.question: C. V. Chandrasekhar was awarded the Padma Bhushan for his contribution in ________.
questions.solution:
Correct answer is__ Bharatanatyam.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• Bharatanatyam

 
 
• In 2011, C V Chandra Shekhar was honoured with the Padma Bhushan by the Government of India for Bharatanatyam.
 
• Bharatnatyam was associated with Devadasi Culture.
 
• Bharatanatyam is a major form of Indian classical dance that originated in Tamil Nadu.
 
• The dance form is also compactly mentioned in Kannada text Manasollasa written by Someshwara III.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/108339d7850dabbeb33b5c3495493f802f53fc2734cdd746f0177780aba0860d.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• Kathakali

 
 
• The purpose of Kathakali Theatre is to tell and honor stories through the medium of dance.​ 
 
• Kathakali or 'story play' took shape in Kerala in southern India in the seventeenth century under the patronage of the prince of Karnataka.
 
 
 
• Manipuri
 
 
• The Manipuri Dance, also known as the Manipuri Raas Leela, is one of the eight major Indian classical dance forms, originating from the state of Manipur.
 
 
 
• Kathak
 
 
• Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.
 
• It is the classical dance form of Uttar Pradesh.
